passages.text: ZTTK Syndrome Expanding the Cardiac Phenotype: A Case of Shone’s Complex With a Novel <italic toggle="yes">SON</italic> Variant and Focused Review of the Cardiac Manifestations in ZTTK Syndrome

Zhu-Tokita-Takenouchi-Kim (ZTTK) syndrome is a rare multisystem neurodevelopmental disorder caused by heterozygous variants in <italic toggle="yes">SON</italic>. <sentence_start/>Presented here is a case of a four-year-old female with multiple rare manifestations including a complex neurodevelopmental disorder, Shone complex and a simple capillary malformation. <sentence_start/>Genetic analysis confirmed a novel frameshift variant in <italic toggle="yes">SON,</italic> which was classified as pathogenic. <sentence_start/>The patient has epilepsy and moderate-to-severe global developmental delay. <sentence_start/>Her epilepsy is well controlled with levetiracetam monotherapy. <sentence_start/>A focused literature review was undertaken and found that cardiac defects are reported in an estimated 22% of cases to date. <sentence_start/>Obstructive left-sided heart lesions are rarely reported, and this is the first reported case of Shone complex in the reported ZTTK patient cohorts. <sentence_start/>Loss-of-function variants in <italic toggle="yes">SON</italic> are implicated in abnormal RNA expression and splicing in genes involved in neural migration and metabolism. <sentence_start/>The literature review did not reveal an increased association between epilepsy in ZTTK patients and that in congenital heart disease compared with ZTTK patients without congenital heart disease, supporting the previous findings that <italic toggle="yes">SON</italic> is likely to be involved in multiple critical biological processes. <sentence_start/>Mitochondrial dysfunction was implicated in previous reports of loss-of-function <italic toggle="yes">SON</italic> variants and supported by the cardiac phenotype in previously reported cases.

Zhu-Tokita-Takenouchi-Kim (ZTTK) syndrome is a rare multisystem neurodevelopmental disorder caused by heterozygous variants in the <italic toggle="yes">SON</italic> gene. <sentence_start/>ZTTK was first described in 2015, a neurodevelopmental disorder with variable manifestations [<citation rid="bib-0001" ref-type="bibr" doi="10.1038/gim.2014.191" pmid="25590979" pmcid="PMC4791490" count="1">1</citation>-<citation rid="bib-0004" ref-type="bibr" doi="10.1016/j.ajhg.2016.06.029" pmid="27545680" pmcid="PMC5011044" count="1">4</citation>]. <sentence_start/>Phenotypic features include seizures, congenital heart disease (CHD), visceral organ abnormalities, genitourinary abnormalities, short stature, musculoskeletal abnormalities, developmental delay, structural brain abnormalities and variable dysmorphic features [<citation rid="bib-0005" ref-type="bibr" doi="10.1038/s41431-021-00960-4" pmid="34521999" pmcid="PMC8904542" count="1">5</citation>]. <sentence_start/>Disease-causing variants in <italic toggle="yes">SON</italic> can cause disruption of transcription/RNA splicing. <sentence_start/>Haploinsufficiency results in dysregulated neural migration and dendritic abnormalities [<citation rid="bib-0006" ref-type="bibr" count="1">6</citation>]. <sentence_start/>Frameshift, nonsense and missense variants have been reported [<citation rid="bib-0005" ref-type="bibr" doi="10.1038/s41431-021-00960-4" pmid="34521999" pmcid="PMC8904542" count="1">5</citation>, <citation rid="bib-0006" ref-type="bibr" count="1">6</citation>]. <sentence_start/>It is ubiquitously expressed in different tissues and organs [<citation rid="bib-0007" ref-type="bibr" doi="10.1186/s13041-020-00622-4" pmcid="PMC7245844" pmid="32448361" count="1">7</citation>]. <sentence_start/>Recently, patients with ZTTK have been described with myocardial injury, cardiomyopathy and metabolic stroke, suggesting that abnormalities of mitochondrial function may contribute to the pathophysiology [<citation rid="bib-0008" ref-type="bibr" doi="10.1172/jci.insight.175053" pmcid="PMC10972584" pmid="38290089" count="1">8</citation>, <citation rid="bib-0009" ref-type="bibr" doi="10.1186/s12887-024-04703-4" pmcid="PMC10985872" pmid="38566089" count="1">9</citation>].

Shone complex is a rare CHD comprising a constellation of left-sided obstructive cardiac lesions including supravalvular mitral membrane, parachute mitral valve, subaortic stenosis and coarctation of the aorta [<citation rid="bib-0010" ref-type="bibr" doi="10.1212/NXG.0000000000200072" pmcid="PMC10166595" pmid="37168776" count="1">10</citation>]. <sentence_start/>It is a rare form of CHD, representing approximately 0.7% of defects [<citation rid="bib-0011" ref-type="bibr" doi="10.1016/0002-9149(63)90098-5" pmid="13988650" count="1">11</citation>]. <sentence_start/>It is commonly diagnosed in infancy but can be diagnosed at various stages of life from the prenatal period into adulthood. <sentence_start/>A single mechanism or genetic aetiology has not been confirmed to cause this condition [<citation rid="bib-0012" ref-type="bibr" doi="10.1016/j.cjca.2016.09.005" pmid="27956040" count="1">12</citation>]. <sentence_start/>The association of Shone complex with ZTTK syndrome has not been previously reported.

We present a case of a female paediatric patient with multiple rare disease manifestations including ZTTK syndrome, Shone complex and a simple capillary malformation. <sentence_start/>This includes a focused review of the cardiac phenotype associated with ZTTK syndrome to examine the evidence and identify associated or causal factors.

A 4-year-old girl was referred to the clinical genetics team because of a complex congenital heart condition, Shone complex. <sentence_start/>The patient had multiple comorbid medical needs including epilepsy, global developmental delay, a simple capillary malformation affecting the face and a duplex left kidney. <sentence_start/>She was born at term following a spontaneous conception. <sentence_start/>Prenatal history included maternal gestational diabetes mellitus that was well controlled with diet. <sentence_start/>There was no maternal medication use or teratogen exposure. <sentence_start/>She weighed 3.03 kg (18th centile) at the time of birth. <sentence_start/>Thirty minutes following birth, the patient became lethargic and cyanotic in appearance and was admitted to the neonatal intensive care unit, where she remained CPAP-dependent for the first week of life. <sentence_start/>She was subsequently diagnosed with Shone complex on echocardiogram during this admission. <sentence_start/>The patient has never required intervention for this and remains well under regular cardiac surveillance. <sentence_start/>Her parents are nonconsanguineous. <sentence_start/>She has two healthy older brothers. <sentence_start/>There is no close family history of cardiac, neurological or neurodevelopmental disorders.

Her seizures began at the age of 1 year, when she presented with status epilepticus secondary to a generalised tonic-clonic seizure. <sentence_start/>She had abnormalities on EEG and was commenced on levetiracetam. <sentence_start/>Since then, she has had two further seizures related to suspected infection. <sentence_start/>There was no evidence of clinical immunodeficiency or recurrent severe infections. <sentence_start/>The patient has a facial capillary venous malformation present since birth. <sentence_start/>She had delayed tooth eruption, and her family noted poor nail growth.

The patient has global developmental delay across all domains. <sentence_start/>Her speech is delayed. <sentence_start/>At the age of 4 years, she could use 2-3 words. <sentence_start/>She is unable to walk but could crawl. <sentence_start/>She could feed herself with her fingers but could not grasp a pencil. <sentence_start/>She was not toileting independently. <sentence_start/>She had a happy demeanour and is stranger aware. <sentence_start/>She could not wave or greet. <sentence_start/>Her hearing and vision were normal.

At the age of 6 years, the family was reviewed again. <sentence_start/>The patient was stable medically, and her epilepsy was well controlled on levetiracetam monotherapy. <sentence_start/>Her current seizure type was absence seizures. <sentence_start/>Her cardiac function remained stable. <sentence_start/>She continued to make developmental progress and could walk with a walking aid. <sentence_start/>She was not speaking sentences but could say 2 or 3 words with meaning (naming family members). <sentence_start/>Her family described her as ‘sweet natured’. <sentence_start/>She was sleeping throughout the night. <sentence_start/>She was not yet toileting independently.

On examination, the patient had down-slanting palpebral fissures. <sentence_start/>She had mild hypertelorism with a flat nasal bridge. <sentence_start/>She was noted to have microdontia, micrognathia and long eyelashes. <sentence_start/>There was a low anterior hairline, and sparse lateral eyebrows were noted. <sentence_start/>The ears were posteriorly rotated. <sentence_start/>There was a capillary venous malformation across the middle section of the face including the nose and over the distribution of the face on the left side of the face involving the maxillary region but sparing the forehead (see patient Figures 1, 2 and 3). <sentence_start/>There was a single café au lait patch 2 × 4 cm on the left forearm. <sentence_start/>There was notable joint hypermobility. <sentence_start/>Ptosis was noted as she grew older but not on initial examination.

Photograph taken at 1 year of age. <sentence_start/>A capillary venous malformation, down-slanting palpebral fissures, long eyelashes, a flat and widened nasal bridge, sparse eyebrows and a low anterior hairline were noted.

Photograph taken at 4 years of age, front view. <sentence_start/>A capillary venous malformation less prominent than at age 1, a broad nasal bridge, a broad and flattened nasal tip, hypertelorism, prognathia, long eyelashes, down-slanting palpebral fissures, ptosis, a prominent lower lip and a thin lateral eyebrow were noted.
Patient side profile showing prognathia and a venous malformation.
Renal ultrasound, 2019: The left kidney had a duplex configuration; otherwise, the kidneys had no other abnormal findings.
Brain MRI, 2020: The brain parenchyma was normal with no intracranial abnormality detected.

EEG, 2020: The EEG showed persistent rhythmic, high-amplitude slowing with occasional broad complex activities over the left posterior greater than mid temporal region. <sentence_start/>This confirmed a focal cortical disturbance in the left posterior greater than mid temporal region.
Array CGH, 2020 (GRCh37): Arr(1-22,X)x2. <sentence_start/>No diagnostic abnormality was detected across 60,000 probes using the Agilent SurePrint G3 platform.

Echocardiogram, 2023: The echocardiogram showed Shone complex. <sentence_start/>The atrial and ventricular were septa intact. <sentence_start/>There was trace mitral and tricuspid regurgitation. <sentence_start/>The descending aorta was mildly hypoplastic.

Ophthalmology assessment showed exotropia of approx. 30 dioptres for near and on cover testing, with exotropia measuring 40 dioptres for distance. <sentence_start/>No obvious field defects were detected, nor was there a refractive error.

A trio exome analysis was completed using Illumina sequencing with an external laboratory partner. <sentence_start/>Sequencing included analysis of the coding regions and conserved splice sites of 23,244 genes by next-generation sequencing (Twist Core Human Exome/Illumina NextSeq/NovaSeq). <sentence_start/>Parentage was confirmed. <sentence_start/>CNV calling was completed with the assay but does not detect balanced arrangements. <sentence_start/>Small variant detection (SNV and indels) sensitivity in the testing was > 99% at a read depth of more than 20x, although mosaic variant calling is limited. <sentence_start/>Variants are classified using the ACMG classification [<citation rid="bib-0013" ref-type="bibr" doi="10.1038/gim.2015.30" pmid="25741868" pmcid="PMC4544753" count="1">13</citation>]. <sentence_start/>A de novo novel pathogenic variant in <italic toggle="yes">SON</italic> was identified, confirming a diagnosis of ZTTK syndrome (see Table 1).

A focused literature review was completed using PubMed Central. <sentence_start/>Search terms included ‘ZTTK’ and ‘ZTTK syndrome’. <sentence_start/>This yielded 51 cases of interest (see Table 2). <sentence_start/>Duplicate reports from review papers or those without a human patient cohort were excluded. <sentence_start/>To describe the cardiac phenotypes in ZTTK, a focused strategy was undertaken to collect phenotype and reported clinical data for those with cardiac manifestations of the disorder during completion of the literature review (see Table 1). <sentence_start/>The variant detected in the patient described above has not previously been reported in the literature.

All cases described had reported developmental delay, and 49% had epilepsy (25/51). <sentence_start/>Cardiac abnormalities were described in 22% of cases (11/51). <sentence_start/>Structural heart defects included tetralogy of Fallot (1/11), atrial septal defect (ASD) (4/11), ventricular septal defect (VSD) (1/11), ASD + VSD (2/11), hypoplastic left heart syndrome (1/11), recurrent myocardial injuries (1/11) and unspecified cardiac abnormalities (1/11). <sentence_start/>The genotype described for 10/11 of these cases was predicted as loss of function, and 1/11 was unspecified. <sentence_start/>Epilepsy was present in 45% of cases (5/11).

This case is a novel report of ZTTK associated with Shone complex. <sentence_start/>Shone complex is associated with left-sided obstructive heart lesions [<citation rid="bib-0010" ref-type="bibr" doi="10.1212/NXG.0000000000200072" pmcid="PMC10166595" pmid="37168776" count="1">10</citation>]. <sentence_start/>For those cases reported in the literature, the most prominent lesions are septal defects (64%), hypoplastic left heart syndrome [<citation rid="bib-0014" ref-type="bibr" doi="10.1002/mgg3.1432" pmcid="PMC7549597" pmid="32705777" count="1">14</citation>] and tetralogy of Fallot [<citation rid="bib-0017" ref-type="bibr" doi="10.3390/children9060869" pmcid="PMC9221680" pmid="35740806" count="1">17</citation>], and these were the two complex lesions reported to date. <sentence_start/>While some features of obstructive heart lesions [<citation rid="bib-0014" ref-type="bibr" doi="10.1002/mgg3.1432" pmcid="PMC7549597" pmid="32705777" count="1">14</citation>] and valvular issues have been reported [<citation rid="bib-0017" ref-type="bibr" doi="10.3390/children9060869" pmcid="PMC9221680" pmid="35740806" count="1">17</citation>], Shone complex or other features such as subaortic stenosis, coarctation, parachute mitral valve or supravalvular mitral ring were not revealed in our review of the literature. <sentence_start/>Epilepsy was not overrepresented in those with CHD in the cohort (45%) compared with epilepsy in the entire cohort (49%). <sentence_start/>Previous reports describe abnormal expression of RNA in genes critical for neural migration in individuals with loss-of-function <italic toggle="yes">SON</italic> variants [<citation rid="bib-0004" ref-type="bibr" doi="10.1016/j.ajhg.2016.06.029" pmid="27545680" pmcid="PMC5011044" count="1">4</citation>]. <sentence_start/>Multiple additional congenital abnormalities were reported across all cases in the literature, which supports the theory that <italic toggle="yes">SON</italic> may be important in various embryonal and developmental processes.

One other case from the literature with CHD [<citation rid="bib-0019" ref-type="bibr" doi="10.1002/ccr3.6529" pmcid="PMC9755635" pmid="36540882" count="1">19</citation>] has an angioma present on the forehead. <sentence_start/>Although it is difficult to compare an angioma with the capillary malformation in our patient, this, in combination with the various congenital and cardiac anomalies represented in ZTTK, may be suggestive that the responsible gene may affect the vascular regulation processes during embryonal development. <sentence_start/>Most commonly, simple capillary malformations are associated with somatic variants in <italic toggle="yes">GNAQ, GNA11, GNA14</italic> and, more rarely, germline or somatic syndromic (e.g., <italic toggle="yes">PIK3CA</italic>) and nonsyndromic conditions [<citation rid="bib-0020" ref-type="bibr" doi="10.1016/j.lpm.2025.104292" pmid="40449788" count="1">20</citation>]. <sentence_start/>Given the location of the capillary lesion, limited management implications and complexity of our case, a somatic biopsy was not pursued. <sentence_start/>It is plausible that this phenomenon may be due to a process unrelated to ZTTK.

The variant in our case is a frameshift variant :c.4723_4729del, and it has not been reported in the literature. <sentence_start/>Loss of function is a known mechanism for ZTTK [<citation rid="bib-0021" ref-type="bibr" count="1">21</citation>]. <sentence_start/>One of the most approximate reported variants to ours in the literature involves a case with a frameshift SON:c.3852_3856delGGTAT variant, detected in a 7-year-old with recurrent myocardial injury, intellectual disability and syndromic features. <sentence_start/>On three occasions, they presented with elevated myocardial enzyme spectrum indicators and T-wave changes or ST-T changes on ECG. <sentence_start/>Echocardiogram on each occasion did not detect other structural or valvular lesions, and interval improvements in the ECG were seen [<citation rid="bib-0009" ref-type="bibr" doi="10.1186/s12887-024-04703-4" pmcid="PMC10985872" pmid="38566089" count="1">9</citation>]. <sentence_start/>The next most approximate and comparable variant in the literature is a de novo frameshift variant SON: c.5334_5335delAG in a female. <sentence_start/>She had neurological signs including mild delayed myelination, enlarged bilateral ventricles and widened frontotemporal extracerebral space. <sentence_start/>She had esotropia and mild facial abnormalities with a flat nasal bridge and a short nose. <sentence_start/>She showed no abnormalities in the heart, genitourinary or skeletal systems. <sentence_start/>There was no evidence of seizures or abnormality noted on EEG in this patient either [<citation rid="bib-0022" ref-type="bibr" doi="10.1002/jdn.10170" pmid="35080253" count="1">22</citation>]. <sentence_start/>This variant is located further toward the 5′ end of the DNA compared with the variant detected in our patient and may contribute to the phenotypic difference. <sentence_start/>Trio whole-exome sequencing in the case did not detect additional variants to explain the phenotype. <sentence_start/>The analysis pipeline filters to include variants that are de novo, predicted high impact variants, compound bilallelic variants, splicing variants, and panels are applied for genes associated with cardiovascular presentations.

It is hypothesised that ZTTK syndrome results in abnormal splicing of mRNAs of cardiac transcription factors or structural proteins [<citation rid="bib-0023" ref-type="bibr" doi="10.1007/s00439-023-02540-6" pmid="36929417" count="1">23</citation>]. <sentence_start/>Abnormal expression and alternative splicing in 11 genes were recorded in blood samples obtained from individuals with loss-of-function <italic toggle="yes">SON</italic> variants. <sentence_start/>These were genes critical for neural migration and metabolism [<citation rid="bib-0004" ref-type="bibr" doi="10.1016/j.ajhg.2016.06.029" pmid="27545680" pmcid="PMC5011044" count="1">4</citation>]. <sentence_start/><italic toggle="yes">IDH2</italic> is one example of a downregulated gene. <sentence_start/>It has previously been associated with cardiac hypertrophy and enhanced oxidative stress in the mitochondria [<citation rid="bib-0024" ref-type="bibr" doi="10.1016/j.freeradbiomed.2014.12.018" pmid="25557279" count="1">24</citation>]. <sentence_start/>It is possibly contributory to recurrent myocardial injuries described in ZTTK [<citation rid="bib-0009" ref-type="bibr" doi="10.1186/s12887-024-04703-4" pmcid="PMC10985872" pmid="38566089" count="1">9</citation>]. <sentence_start/><italic toggle="yes">PCK2</italic> is another gene reported to have abnormal expression [<citation rid="bib-0004" ref-type="bibr" doi="10.1016/j.ajhg.2016.06.029" pmid="27545680" pmcid="PMC5011044" count="1">4</citation>]. <sentence_start/><italic toggle="yes">PCK2</italic> has previously been implicated in cardiomyocyte metabolism, and abnormal RNA splicing of this gene may be implicated in the development of cardiac hypertrophy or may be vital in other developmental cardiac processes [<citation rid="bib-0024" ref-type="bibr" doi="10.1016/j.freeradbiomed.2014.12.018" pmid="25557279" count="1">24</citation>]. <sentence_start/>In our case, it is possible that abnormal early development of cardiomyocytes caused downstream structural events, which led to the development of Shone complex [<citation rid="bib-0004" ref-type="bibr" doi="10.1016/j.ajhg.2016.06.029" pmid="27545680" pmcid="PMC5011044" count="1">4</citation>, <citation rid="bib-0024" ref-type="bibr" doi="10.1016/j.freeradbiomed.2014.12.018" pmid="25557279" count="1">24</citation>, <citation rid="bib-0025" ref-type="bibr" doi="10.1016/j.redox.2021.102094" pmcid="PMC8379496" pmid="34418597" count="1">25</citation>]. <sentence_start/>Other examples of RNA splicing regulatory genes causing cardiac phenotypes (congenital heart defects and cardiomyopathy) include <italic toggle="yes">EFTUD2</italic> [<citation rid="bib-0026" ref-type="bibr" doi="10.1016/j.ajhg.2011.12.023" pmid="22305528" pmcid="PMC3276671" count="1">26</citation>], <italic toggle="yes">RBM20</italic> [<citation rid="bib-0027" ref-type="bibr" doi="10.1016/j.ijcard.2025.133350" pmid="40339755" count="1">27</citation>, <citation rid="bib-0028" ref-type="bibr" doi="10.3390/jcm10184101" pmcid="PMC8468976" pmid="34575212" count="1">28</citation>], <italic toggle="yes">TXNL4A</italic> [<citation rid="bib-0029" ref-type="bibr" doi="10.1038/ejhg.2017.107" pmid="28905882" pmcid="PMC5602009" count="1">29</citation>] and <italic toggle="yes">SF3B4</italic> [<citation rid="bib-0030" ref-type="bibr" doi="10.1016/j.ajhg.2012.04.004" pmid="22541558" pmcid="PMC3376638" count="1">30</citation>].

From a management perspective, ZTTK syndrome requires a multidisciplinary approach. <sentence_start/>Cardiac care is one aspect, alongside neurologic, developmental, ophthalmologic, orthopaedic and gastroenterological care. <sentence_start/>Regarding cardiac management, no ZTTK-specific guidelines have been described in case reports. <sentence_start/>In reports where therapeutic intervention was described [<citation rid="bib-0009" ref-type="bibr" doi="10.1186/s12887-024-04703-4" pmcid="PMC10985872" pmid="38566089" count="1">9</citation>, <citation rid="bib-0015" ref-type="bibr" doi="10.1111/pde.14113" pmid="32045494" count="1">15</citation>, <citation rid="bib-0017" ref-type="bibr" doi="10.3390/children9060869" pmcid="PMC9221680" pmid="35740806" count="1">17</citation>, <citation rid="bib-0019" ref-type="bibr" doi="10.1002/ccr3.6529" pmcid="PMC9755635" pmid="36540882" count="1">19</citation>], lesions have mostly been addressed according to standard paediatric cardiology practices. <sentence_start/>Hudec and Kosinova [<citation rid="bib-0017" ref-type="bibr" doi="10.3390/children9060869" pmcid="PMC9221680" pmid="35740806" count="1">17</citation>] report that careful preoperative assessment, including cardiac assessment, is crucial in these patients. <sentence_start/>Individualised care planning may be required, particularly for hypotonia and dysmorphism, which can affect airway and operative care. <sentence_start/>In clinical practice, considerations for investigations, including cardiac imaging, and assessment for features of mitochondrial dysfunction may be worthwhile in symptomatic cases. <sentence_start/>This may be an important consideration given the implication of this gene in mitochondrial metabolic regulation; however, the evidence regarding <italic toggle="yes">SON</italic> variants continues to emerge [<citation rid="bib-0004" ref-type="bibr" doi="10.1016/j.ajhg.2016.06.029" pmid="27545680" pmcid="PMC5011044" count="1">4</citation>, <citation rid="bib-0009" ref-type="bibr" doi="10.1186/s12887-024-04703-4" pmcid="PMC10985872" pmid="38566089" count="1">9</citation>, <citation rid="bib-0024" ref-type="bibr" doi="10.1016/j.freeradbiomed.2014.12.018" pmid="25557279" count="1">24</citation>, <citation rid="bib-0025" ref-type="bibr" doi="10.1016/j.redox.2021.102094" pmcid="PMC8379496" pmid="34418597" count="1">25</citation>].
